subject.title: Gateway should not fail to start when optional ElevenLabs/TTS API key is missing

question: Should `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` and related optional TTS provider SecretRefs be non-fatal at Gateway startup while gateway auth and other required runtime secrets remain fail-closed?
rationale: The code can support a repair, but choosing which configured SecretRefs are optional at startup changes the product's fail-closed boundary and needs maintainer intent.

options.title: Degrade optional TTS secrets
options.body: Treat unresolved optional TTS provider keys as configured-unavailable at startup and keep the Gateway running, while preserving strict startup failure for gateway auth and explicitly required secrets.

options.title: Keep all configured refs strict
options.body: Preserve the current fail-closed startup behavior for every collected active SecretRef, accepting that optional TTS misconfiguration can take down the Gateway.

options.title: Only skip inactive providers
options.body: Resolve only provider keys that are selected by active TTS config, which reduces some false failures but still fails startup when the selected optional TTS provider key is missing.

recommendation.title: Degrade optional TTS secrets
recommendation.body: Treat unresolved optional TTS provider keys as configured-unavailable at startup and keep the Gateway running, while preserving strict startup failure for gateway auth and explicitly required secrets.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision centers on the SecretRef runtime framework and active/inactive assignment semantics introduced in the broad SecretRef coverage work.
